symptom: In a headerless (mdl 0) script, any parse error on a line containing `\'` carries "Under mdl 1 a backslash is an ordinary character, so `\'` ends the string literal" — but under mdl 0 the backslash escapes the apostrophe and the literal does NOT end there, so the advice explains a failure that did not happen
cause: The #732 backslash hint keys only on the source line containing `\'`; enhanceErrorMessage never knew which escape rule the script was lexed with
insight: A hint that explains a version-dependent rule must be told the version: the escape rule is decided once per script in newScriptStream, so read it back with parser.HasStrictEscapes(chars) in build() and hand it to the listener — do not re-scan the header. Found as a side finding while fixing #1533/#1514; the mdl 1 test never caught it because it only ever ran under `mdl 1;`.
